notes.title: DevLog #10 - 300 wishlists!
notes.content: [h2]300 wishlists![/h2][p]After 5.5 months of development, I gained 300 wishlists. Thanks to all wishlisters! A rather large portion of that came during the last 5 days when I released a new trailer, so check that out![/p][previewyoutube="_whezwsC4UI;full"][/previewyoutube][p]There's also a new updated gameplay video:[/p][previewyoutube="RavI50LBwRc;full"][/previewyoutube][p]Sadly, I also got a cold and couldn't work for a few days so there aren't as many updates as I'd like there to be...[/p][p][/p][h3][b]Changes:[/b][/h3][p][/p][h3][b]Robots[/b][/h3][list][*][p]I refined the health system. Previously, there were 4 different components, each with their own health, which was too UI-heavy and complex. Wasn't happy at all so I went back to a simple 1-Health-bar system. The subsystems still exist and can be damaged. But instead of a separate health bar they are now simply damaged or not.[/p][/*][*][p]Job queue now allows to delete and reorder existing jobs.[/p][/*][*][p]Energy Refill can be individually set for each robot. Changes of these settings create a job, that needs to be performed by a crew member before becoming active.[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][h3][b]Crew Management[/b][/h3][list][*][p]Eating and sleeping were set at the start of the day, which wasn't a good idea as it takes away too much control. Now, you can send each character to sleep or to eat separately. [/p][/*][*][p]Added a few more traits:[/p][list][*][p]Generator specialist: 10% bonus generator output when assigned to the generator station[/p][/*][/list][list][*][p]Robot Engineer: 15% faster on performing jobs in the robot bay[/p][/*][/list][/*][/list][p][/p][h3][b]Combat[/b][/h3][list][*][p]Changed the ranged monster to a different model since I didn't like this weird scorpion...[/p][/*][*][p]New monster designs (only partly implemented):[/p][list][*][p]2nd ranged monster that buffs surrounding monsters (screenshot)[/p][/*][*][p]Artillery monster (maybe?)[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Defender ability: Shield Reload[/p][/*][*][p]Ammunition system:[/p][list][*][p]Manual reload ability[/p][/*][*][p]Automatic reload when ammo is depleted[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Changed the vision drone (removes Fog of War) to a stationary scanner with a fancy animation (screenshot)[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45611111/fb7f1c4ca5b16e8cbd0bc054f97c884f2a20921a.jpg"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45611111/06ef07d886106b4ff01ab0301fe7a9dc132cc5da.jpg"][/img][/p][p][/p][p][/p][h3]Next steps:[/h3][p]My main goal now is to finally have an alpha build, which (SURPRISINGLY!) takes a long time, if I keep adding new stuff to the game.[/p][p][/p][p]Therefore, I will add the most important functionalities, which include:[/p][list][*][p]Research[/p][/*][*][p]Basic Main menu[/p][/*][*][p]Main goal (Basic story of the game)[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][h3]See you in 2 weeks![/h3]

notes.title: DevLog #9 - So many changes and updates!
notes.content: [h2]Way too long for a DevLog...[/h2][p][/p][p]Finally getting closer to a real alpha build that includes all mechanics and systems on an at least basic level! There are so many new things that from now on I will have bi-monthly devlogs again.[/p][p]I tuned down social media activity and focused more on the game. [/p][p][/p][h3][b]New Features - Overview:[/b][/h3][list][*][p]Home base refined: I removed a room I had no real use for (machine room) and rather refined the other ones.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45611111/172f0fb4212c757b9aa7b5b02b41fda2b409fd9e.jpg"][/img][/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p][/p][list][*][p]Added functionality to the control room: Analysis of weather, monster nests, and alien ore before going to the outpost.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45611111/87182e3e49220f6db9d6577ca5c22e43c1ce0a52.jpg"][/img][/p][p][/p][/*][/list][p][/p][list][*][p]Added Mining! Get your mining drone ready and mine this mysterious alien ore[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45611111/c0e5c78ffc2293a8b54f36e392c635781182bb9e.jpg"][/img][/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p][/p][list][*][p]Added monster nests and aggression system (orange bar on the left)[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45611111/db535812313df9e4330148c4fe2d543aa02e7d58.jpg"][/img][/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p][/p][p][/p][list][*][p]Ranged monster. High attack damage but low HP.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45611111/be4ee08f06e828d9ae9f2fb4da7540fc22e10678.jpg"][/img][/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p][/p][p][/p][p][/p][list][*][p]Robot Bay implemented. Manage your robots, assign abilities, repair, etc.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45611111/65d82b1e77abdef65a6382ecc613db0c6d522543.jpg"][/img][/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p][/p][p][/p][list][*][p]2 robot archetypes: Striker (fast & low HP) and Defender (slow & high HP). Repairs and ability changes create jobs in job queues[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45611111/8db7283b5191063f63e758bbe74f24c054092bd4.jpg"][/img][/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p][/p][p][/p][list][*][p]Monster AI update: More natural movement / flanking instead of walking in a straight line[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45611111/68bb0478286a070a8fe494b2104799753430427a.jpg"][/img][/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p][/p][p][/p][list][*][p]Evac Zone at the Outpost: Leave robots behind if neccessary for the survival of the rest[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45611111/7217c4d36f4cad78b737b9736ca2d2b711fbc836.jpg"][/img][/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p][/p][list][*][p]Planning Mode for your trip to the outpost. Analyze weather, monster nests and ore locations and plan accordingly.[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45611111/a2d60afb18bc47730f2da721fb80fcdc65749c2d.jpg"][/img][/p][p] [/p][/*][/list][p][/p][h2][b]New Features - Details:[/b][/h2][p][/p][h3][b]Robots[/b][/h3][p][b][u]Archetypes:[/u][/b][/p][p]Robots are divided into 2 archetypes:[/p][list][*][p]Striker (fast / low HP)[/p][/*][*][p]Defender (slow / high HP)[/p][/*][/list][p]Based on weapon loadout (not implemented yet) and abilities, the player can "create" subclasses, for example a sniper or a tank. However, striker and defenders have different abilities and loadout possibilities. Strikers are used for fast recon, flank attacks, and high damage output while Defenders are used for crowd control, zone defense and damage absorption.[/p][p][/p][p][b][u]Subsystems:[/u][/b][/p][p]Robots have 4 subsystems (as mentioned in the last devlog) and I implemented a damage distribution system and penalties if the subsystems's health falls below 25%:[/p][list][*][p][b]Head (Vision - Attack range and vision range)[/b] - Penalty: 50% less range[/p][/*][*][p][b]Arms (Damage)[/b] - Penalty: 50% less damage[/p][/*][*][p][b]Legs (Movement)[/b] - Penalties:[/p][p]-> Striker: Running animation switches to walking animation: Speed goes down from 9 to 3.5.[/p][p]-> Defender: Only has walking animation: Animation is slowed down by 30%. Speed goes down from 3 to 2.1[/p][/*][*][p][b]Core (Abilities)[/b] - Penalty: Abilities can't be used anymore.[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p][b][u]Energy:[/u][/b][/p][p]Robots require energy to function when they are at the outpost.[/p][list][*][p]Permanent energy decrease (+ weather multiplier if applicable - [i]Ion Storm[/i])[/p][/*][*][p]Abilities (for example Laser or Shield)[/p][/*][/list][p]If a robot's energy is depleted, he shuts down immediately and cannot be used anymore.[/p][p](Not implemented yet: By replenishing energy with an [i]emergency battery cell[/i], the robot can be restarted.)[/p][p][/p][p]Energy is replenished at the home base. However, energy is a resource created by the generator. Always using all available robots for a trip to the outpost will result in an energy deficit.[/p][p][/p][p][b][u]Robot Bay:[/u][/b][/p][p]Visual update for the robot bay. [/p][p]A maximum of 9 robots can be managed simultaneously.[/p][list][*][p]Each robot is assigned to a station slot.[/p][/*][*][p]Energy is replenished when robots are back at the base (They can also be left at the outpost).[/p][/*][*][p]Energy is replenished over night for robots that do not join the player at the outpost[/p][/*][/list][p](Not implemented yet: Since energy is a scarce resource, the player will be able to selectively activate or deactive energy loading for each station slot. This creates a task that needs to be finished by a character before the changes apply.)[/p][p][/p][p][b][u]Job Queue:[/u][/b][/p][p]Each change to a robot [/p][list][*][p]adding an ability[/p][/*][*][p]switching an ability[/p][/*][*][p]removing an ability[/p][/*][*][p]repairing a subsystem[/p][/*][*][p]upgrading a subsystem (not implemented yet)[/p][/*][/list][p]creates a job in a job queue for each robot station. This creates a task for a character. In addition, repairs and upgrades also cost [i]building material[/i].[/p][p](Not implemented yet: Jobs can be stopped or reordered. All active jobs are reset if a robot goes to the outpost.)[/p][p][/p][h3][b]Monster[/b][/h3][p][b][u]Monster Nests:[/u][/b][/p][p]There are several fixed monster nests in the world, which spawn a few monsters continuously every x seconds. Not all of them are active everytime.[/p][p][/p][p]They are different from each other regarding:[/p][list][*][p]Spawn time (the time between 2 consecutive spawns)[/p][/*][*][p]Monster type[/p][/*][*][p]Amount of monsters in each spawn (random value between min value and max value + jitter)[/p][/*][*][p]Aggression level (increases min and max spawn amount)[/p][/*][*][p]Max aggression level (meaning, some nests can become more dangerous than others over time)[/p][/*][/list][p](Not implemented yet: The player can [i]disable[/i] a monster nest by attacking it / performing a task. If not disabled, it stays active and becomes a bigger problem each time. When attacking a nest, an alarm attracts large monster crowds, which requires a player to carefully plan a nest attack.)[/p][p](Not implemented yet: Regularly, additional nests are activated so the player is advised to disable/destroy at least some of them.)[/p][p](Not implemented / modeled yet: The world can be destroyed in parts. For example, a bridge may give access to a resourceful location for the player, but also create a pathway for a very dangerous monster nest. At some point, the player may decide to destroy the bridge.)[/p][p][/p][p][b][u]Ranged monster:[/u][/b][/p][p]A scorpion-like monster performs fast high-ranged attacks and should be focused by the player. [/p][p]2 other enemy types planned (not implemented yet):[/p][list][*][p]Mostly stationary energy-consuming monster: only active during [i]Ion Storms. P[/i]layer needs to scan to find it and kill it for special bonuses[/p][/*][*][p]Heavyly armored monster that leaves toxic gas behind after dying. Player needs to plan carefully where to kill it. An armor system is already implemented.[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p][b][u]Monster AI:[/u][/b][/p][p]Previously, monsters always ran the shortest path, which led to unnatural movment, i.e, all monster ran in a line. Now, monsters pick a point in a radius around their actual target, which automatically leads to different paths for each monster. In open spaces, this also leads to flank attacks.[/p][p](Not implemented yet: Different monsters behave differently. Weather may also change the AI.)[/p][p](Partly implemented yet: Monsters don't just attack the closest target but rather they pick a target based on [i]aggro[/i]. Aggro can be created in different ways, for example a character that performs a specific task might create a lot of aggro, which requires the player to defend it carefully.)[/p][p](Not implemented yet: Monster patrols / Monster defense in specific areas)[/p][p][b][u]Aggression:[/u][/b][/p][p]In addition to the local aggression level of the monster nest aggression level, this aggression level is added as well and can be changed by the player, whereas the aggression level of a monster nest cannot be directly controlled.[/p][p]Killing monsters creates global aggression (seen as the red slider on the left in the screenshots). Mining also creates a large amount of aggression so the player needs to plan carefully if the current trip will be focused on mining or not.[/p][p](Not implemented yet: The player should be able to decrease the global aggression level or lower the rise of aggression by performing tasks with the characters or similar)[/p][p](Not implemented yet: When the global aggression level reaches a new level, a large monster wave appears.)[/p][p][/p][h3][b]Control Room[/b][/h3][p]Planning the outpost phase will be an important aspect of the game. Based on several factors, you should decide how many and which robots the player deploys (while also paying attention to their individual health and energy statuses), and which characters to send to the outpost based on their skills and current status (fatigue, hunger, stress).[/p][p][b][u]Tasks:[/u][/b][/p][p]Currently, the control room has 3 separate tasks to scan the outpost for:[/p][list][*][p]Weather: Shows, which weather is active during the next trip.[/p][/*][*][p]Alien Ore: Shows the location of all ores. The player only has limited time to mine the ore, otherwise it disappears due to instability.[/p][/*][*][p]Monster nest (scanning not implemented yet): Shows the status (if active or not), details (aggression level, monster type, etc...), and position of monster nests[/p][/*][/list][p]The player does not have to perform all of these tasks. In fact, since time is limited, oftentimes the player won't be able to. Every decision should be a trade-off. Information is important, especially when you plan a more dangerous trip where you try to destroy a monster nest. [/p][p][/p][p][b][u]Weather system:[/u][/b][/p][p]On each trip to the outpost, the weather might change ([u]not during[/u] the trip). Currently, 2 weather types are implemented and 1 more is done in the next few days.[/p][list][*][p]Clear Sky: no modifiers[/p][/*][*][p]Ion Storm: Energy decrease of robots multiplied by 3[/p][/*][*][p]Quakes (not implemented yet): Regular earthquakes so robots cannot correctly adjust their focus [/p][p]-> damage by robots decreased by 20%[/p][/*][/list][p]I also plan to add 1 or 2 weather types with positive effects or rather positive [u]AND[/u] negative effects.[/p][p](Not implemented yet: For these and further weather types, I plan to add components for robots to counteract the negative effects.)[/p][p][/p][p][b][u]Outpost preview:[/u][/b][/p][p]The player can check the outpost any time and see the status (based on completed control room tasks) and task details of the outpost to decide what to do next.[/p][p]The player can analyze:[/p][list][*][p]in which area the ore is[/p][/*][*][p]which tasks are active and which requirements they have[/p][/*][*][p]The devlog is getting too long...[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][h3][b]Mining[/b][/h3][p]Mining will be the player's main option to get building material. In contrast to fast paced RTS-games, mining in Frost Protocol is slow and dangerous. The player needs to defend the mining drone because the aggression level is increasing quickly while mining.[/p][p]Mining requires planning:[/p][list][*][p]Where is the closest alien ore?[/p][/*][*][p]Which monster nests are next to it? Are they active?[/p][/*][*][p]How difficult is the area to defend?[/p][/*][/list][p](Not implemented yet: Research to increase mining speed, drone speed, drone capacity, aggression level decrease)[/p][p][/p][h3][b]Character traits[/b][/h3][p]Initially, I planned to have a very deep character system with emotions and relationships. But the complexity of such a system (if done correctly) might be too much (especially at this stage). So for now, I plan to reduce this complexity and focus on a few mechanics.[/p][p]I implemented simple traits (ok, just 1 for now). For example [i]Green Thumb[/i], which reduces the time required for all tasks on the food creator station by 15%.[/p][p]These traits will be used for tasks at the outposts as well. But I need to find out, how to combine this with the skills that are also already implemented. Currently, 4 skills are available:[/p][list][*][p]Engineering[/p][/*][*][p]Physics[/p][/*][*][p]Biology[/p][/*][*][p]IT[/p][/*][/list][p]These skills are used as requirements for the tasks at the outpost, i.e., a character requires a min level in a skill to perform a specific task. [/p][p][/p][h3][b]Minor changes[/b][/h3][list][*][p]Evacuation zone: Robots may be left behind if they are not in the evac zone when ending the trip. Characters will die if they stay at the outpost.[/p][/*][*][p]Stations in the home base keep running during the trip (robots loading in the robot bay / plants growing in the life support station /...)[/p][/*][*][p]Added 1 tactical resource (no name or purpose, yet). I'll either remove it in the future or use it as some kind of last resort resource during difficult times. [/p][/*][*][p]UI changes: Time is displayed as a clock instead of a slider and several other even smaller UI changes...[/p][p][/p][/*][/list][p][/p][h3]Next steps:[/h3][list][*][p]Everything above mentioned as "Not implemented yet".[/p][/*][*][p]Characters: Hunger, fatigue, stress, and how these values change their behaviour (penalties on tasks or slower movement, etc.)[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][h3]See you in 2 weeks![/h3]

notes.title: 4 months of development!
notes.content: [h1]4 months of development![/h1][p]I took a few days off to have a creative pause so there are not as many new things to see this time...[/p][p]Also, I had a few early alpha playtests and the feedback is worth gold! So rather than implenting new systems, I even removed some and refined the core gameplay.[/p][p]During the last weeks and months, I implemented many many many systems and mechanics that were floating around in my head. The plan was to test lots of things and see what works well and what doesn't so for now everything is going as planned.[/p][p][/p][h2][b]What did I remove and why?[/b][/h2][h3]Crafting[/h3][p]I had implemented a basic crafting system to create items, such as explosives. This meant, I had to have crafting materials (many different ones, otherwise it's pretty senseless) and crafting recipes. This meant a lot of work and a lot of balancing later on. At the same time (and much more important), I implemented base building for the outpost. This is part of the core gameplay: Explore, expand, defend. To build new buildings, I implemented a simple resource "building material". This led to a weird system where I had this macro-level building material and micro-level crafting materials, which I wasn't happy about. Crafting was implemented to enable items for characters on expeditions but this can be solved without crafting - simply by having unlimited items or find them on the expedition.[/p][p][/p][h3]Inventory[/h3][p]No crafting -> no inventory required. Since I want to keep items in general, there will be simple slots for the characters.[/p][p][/p][h2][b]What did I change?[/b][/h2][p][/p][h3]Eating, sleeping, and stress[/h3][p]Eating, sleeping, and stress were handled by a value between 0 and 100. This was too much micro-management and didn't add to the gameplay.[/p][p]Now, the main stat to keep in mind is STRESS - level 0 - 5. Stress is increased / reduces by 1 or more levels by events / decisions. Hunger and Fatigue is not removed but handled differently than before. [/p][p]At the start of the day, the player can decide, which character gets to eat or sleep.[/p][p]Eating options:[/p][list][*][p]Normal ->   -1 stress[/p][/*][*][p]Ration ->     0 stress  +  status effect ("slighty hungry")[/p][/*][*][p]No food ->  +1 stress + status effect ("hungry")[/p][/*][/list][p]Sleeping options:[/p][list][*][p]Sleep ->   -1 stress  [/p][/*][*][p]Don't sleep ->  0 stress  [/p][/*][/list][p]At the end of the day, the player can decide, which character goes on an expedition and who goes to sleep. Depending on who slept during the day, the status effect ("tired") is applied.[/p][p]High stress levels, hunger, and fatigue affect the skill of the characters.[/p][p][/p][h3]Robots[/h3][p]Definition of robot class and damage system and related mechanics[/p][olist][*][p]Head (Vision): Defines the range of the robot (shooting and sight)[/p][/*][*][p]Arms (Accuracy): Defines the damage of the robot[/p][/*][*][p]Legs (Movement): Defines the speed of the robot[/p][/*][*][p]Core (Abilities): Defines if abilities can be used[/p][/*][/olist][p]Damage during combat is split between these 4 components. At 50% damage, each component creates a penalty.[/p][p][/p][p][/p][h3]Combat[/h3][p]Only defending could be boring later on. Therefore, I'm working on a concept for monster nests. There, monster waves are spawned. If the player waits too long, more nests spawn and the monster waves become more dangerous. Attacking and destroying monster nests is dangerous as well, since monster defend them and patrol around them.[/p][p]This leads to a healthy balance of defense and attack, which requires the player to think about robot selection and their loadout at the start of an expedition.[/p][p][/p][p][/p][h3]Small changes[/h3][list][*][p]Bug fixes regarding enemy AI[/p][/*][*][p]Bug fixes regarding pathfinding[/p][/*][*][p]Selection of robots before starting an expedition[/p][/*][*][p]Showing existing robots in the base[/p][/*][*][p]Restructuring of the base[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][h3]Next steps:[/h3][list][*][p]Implementation of monster nests[/p][/*][*][p]Adding more monster types[/p][/*][/list]

notes.title: Devlog #6 - Major Update
notes.content: [p]3 weeks since my last update. Time flies when you work all the time... For those interested in seeing updates more often, check my other social media stuff. [/p][p][/p][p]So now, it's 10 weeks into development. The biggest change is that I switched to real-time from turn-based. I had to rework all concepts to fit this new system so there's not that much in regard to new mechanics or visuals. Most of the work is under the hood.[/p][p]Why did I do this? Turn-based felt boring. If you look at the gameplay video, your main goal will be to defend your crew / certain positions. In turn-based, this meant: Shoot / Use abilities -> next turn -> enemies move closer -> Repeat[/p][p]Also, it made the game too tactical and strategic, whereas the atmosphere I want to create should be more dangerous and direct. There still will be a lot of strategic components to combat but they are implemented differently. Missions can / must be planned beforehand (analyze the map / tasks / spawnpoints, choose your crew / robots and their loadouts, etc.). [/p][p][/p][p][/p][p]New Features / Changes:[/p][list][*][p]As mentioned: Turn-based -> Real-time[/p][p]→ Uploaded a gameplay clip for combat[/p][/*][*][p]More atmosphere:[/p][p]→ Added a ground fog, better wind "clouds", darkened the color palette a bit[/p][/*][*][p]Changed the task system[/p][p]→ Task have requirements (e.g. "Task: Restore Energy" must come before "Task: Activate Turret")[/p][/*][*][p]Map visuals:[/p][p]→ Added a base on the tutorial mission to make the map feel more alive.[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p][b]Whats next?[/b][/p][p]Still the same as last time: Highest priority: I really need to start early alpha playtests! [/p][p][/p][p][b]Conclusion:[/b][/p][p]I'm very happy with the change to real-time. Fits my vision of the game. [/p][p]Have a nice day, guys![/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45611111/2b436f37870315eb8b5c1a344844f132bbaef2ab.jpg"][/img][/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45611111/58b9dc4d66f0e76227cc4b170aa7c2e4ebd464ef.jpg"][/img][/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45611111/6b1703d115d906e8b85d36dc0b56ec0cbc79552c.jpg"][/img][/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45611111/c879c2e94d514ac9152a3d74bfd213fbc0d7d91b.jpg"][/img][/p][p][/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45611111/375af05054cb01334c366faca068e9aedfc9fcc9.jpg"][/img][/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45611111/5ee90652f4f8abe11eb97b0a34ef2825d5976992.jpg"][/img][/p][p][/p][p][/p]

notes.title: Devlog #5 - First closed alpha playtest ready soon!
notes.content:
Hi guys!

Just a quick update. It takes so much time posting daily on Bluesky, Twitter, YouTube and Tiktok (and learning how to make the content better) that I didn't bother with a new devlog but this here is not for community building but rather to structure my thoughts, ideas, and give you more insights into that. So here we go!

7 weeks into development.

[b]
New Features / Changes:[/b]
- New title: Frost Protocol
- Cinematic Trailer
- Tutorial mission
- Base layout 
- Job system in base
- Task UI
- New combat abilities + UI updates

[b]Details:[/b]
- Frost Protocol: There is a TV show and a novel titled "Station 11" so I decided to change the name of my game
→ Steam art rework. What do you think?

- Cinematic Trailer
→ Check it out! It's on the steam page and should give you a feeling for the atmosphere I'm going for in this game.

- Tutorial mission
→ The first mission should immediately show you what this game is about. Robot abilities for example are limited but they are not that important at the start. Sacrifice and tough decisions are!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45611111/bb05497ad6aa7a9761cfb9d9a51b2a8501959a7c.jpg[/img]


- Base layout 
→ Basic base layout is finished, but unpolished yet. But now I know (more or less) what stations I will have in the game.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45611111/d2a26df5b96da2320e97dd97cf2c3375f40e82df.jpg[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45611111/a245c21a4310f9dbfeb38b999d092b95bfb11ed8.jpg[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45611111/2a457dd3c8b1394cac380a1254eaa07a0f6676a3.jpg[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45611111/cc53fc0729f44ac5608b4d04e4124c077dc7b142.jpg[/img]

- Job system in base
→ Each job is categorized into one of the skills (Engineering, Physics, Biology, IT / Computer) and requires a certain amounts of points to be finished. Assigning a crew member costs 1 AP and adds the skill level of the crew member to the progress of the job
→ This needs more detail since I'm not really happy with the system so far.

- Tasks UI
→ Updated the Task UI on expeditions and added sound effects. Tasks are skill-based but depending on the skill difference between the crew member skill and the task requirement (soft requirement) there are chances for Failure (no progress), Success (+1 progress), and Crit Success (+2 progress). 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45611111/f481f5895f35f597cf19883f920d4e5d5d37f545.jpg[/img]

- New combat abilities + UI updates
→ Added a cone attack for the tanky tank. Close range but high damage. I also added visual indicators for the Line Attack (need a better name for that...) and the Cone Attack
- New combat abilities + UI updates
→ Added a mine that can be triggered in the player phase (Apparently, monsters hate explosions and die...)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45611111/9b225839b29ca7b53d9a00456e8c49796b83b3c2.jpg[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45611111/2123db2f0442c6c48b56961a7f581aff43ca6ed4.jpg[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45611111/d9ddb573c26217f8f28e2a017351b3cc18ef241c.jpg[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45611111/286db03792909dc2442a11e9acdcb11526e7a5d4.jpg[/img]

[b]Design Decisions:[/b]
- The combat system needs a rework on the conceptual level, which is what I was working on in the tutorial mission. "Only" defending is too boring imo so the map design needs to be in a way that it forces the player to move. It should be:
→ START: control the spawn points for a few turns but enemies will overwhelm you eventually
→ This gives your crew members time to finish tasks close to the spawn points
→ Retreat to tasks further away / Finished tasks open doorways to new areas
→ Repeat

[b]Whats next?[/b]
Highest priority: I really need to start early alpha playtests! I replayed the first mission so often that I lost all objectivity and can't tell anymore if it's interesting to play or not.

Conclusion:
Social Media is a HORRIBLE GRIND! But the (very few) interactions and conversations with the viewers were worth it! :)

For more gifs and images or videos, check out social media stuff (I'm posting daily):

notes.title: Devlog #4: Combat system updates
notes.content:
[h1]DevLog #4 – Combat system updates[/h1]
Hi guys!

Why am I starting with Devlog #4? Older devlogs are on itch.io (https://atlas-corp.itch.io/station-11)
But from now on, I'll post each devlog here as well.

This week, i solely worked on the combat system or rather everything related to the expeditions (and I actually stayed with turn-based instead of realtime!) The combat actually seems fun now, even though replayed it dozens and dozens of times...

[h2]New Features:[/h2]
[list]
[*] Combat Abilities
[*] Better pathfinding / Simulataneous movement of enemies
[*] Task system updates
[/list]


[h3]Details:[/h3]
[list]
[*] 2D grid system for pathfinding 
→ Changed to A* for better performance
[*] Turn manager
→ All enemies first decide on their path and then start to move -> no waiting for dozens of enemies to move one after another! (This took MOST of the time...)

[*] Combat abilites: including UI, animation, sound
→ Reload: Uses 1 magazine to reload ammo
→ Line Attack: attacks monsters in a single line (Cooldown 1 turn)
→ Shock Attack: stuns all enemies in a circular range for 1 turn (Cooldown 3 turns)
→ Single attack: High dmg attack on a single enemy
[*] 2 different enemy types with different dmg and movement range
[*] Basic armor system for enemies
[*] Tasks on expeditions
→ Tasks have skill requirements (Engineering, Physics, Biology, etc..) and a duration
→ When a character performs a task, it can lead to a
→ Failure: No progress
→ Success: -1 duration
→ Crit Success: -2 duration
→ Chances are based on character skills vs task requirement
[*] UI changes / updates
→ Select characters and robots by UI icons
→ Robot: show abilites / cooldowns / ammo / magazines
[*] Map updates: more details: rocks, plants, etc.

[/list]



[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45611111/26e697c9d44b354add0beec7cb499636e911c7eb.jpg[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45611111/cdf5a7d01107327a1653888b41b8e37c29ac7272.jpg[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45611111/67668c4f2ac277e40932ecef177c1a4142b48865.jpg[/img]



[h2]Design Decisions:[/h2]
Decision #1 - Visit expeditions once vs multiple times
At first, I planned for the player to revisit an expedition, if it wasn't finished the first time, which leads to balancing HELL! Now, you have 1 chance -> higher stakes, easier balancing, better gameplay.

[h2]Whats next?[/h2]
The next days, I want to focus on the base management. After that's finished (at a basic level), the gameloop is done and I can start a few alpha test with playtesters.
[h2]
Conclusion:[/h2]

Very happy with the combat system and the atmosphere that it's creating.

Wishlist the game, if you like it so far!


For more gifs and images, check out my Bluesky or Twitter accounts (I'm posting daily):

https://bsky.app/profile/station11game.bsky.social
